note: A 30-year-old research engineer at a research institute reads as professional-equivalent on the occupation test, health is clearly the neglected area rather than a crisis, and at 84 kg against a 76 kg target with a daily 6,000-8,000 steps and a gym habit he is a good-to-great case rather than a rescue. Income is the material miss and it is a pure gap in discovery — no affordability question was asked at any point, no price was quoted, and a salaried researcher is not evidently the business-owner-or-physician bracket the ICP describes. 'not_deconditioned' is recorded as a miss on a technicality worth noting rather than on substance: he is not 50 lb overweight and not gym-averse, but he has never sustained a kettlebell routine for more than a week and asked for a one-session-a-week entry point, so the programme's three-to-four-day baseline is above his demonstrated floor. The criterion that actually decided this call — willingness to commit to a fixed regimen — is not in the stated ICP at all, and this is the second call in the batch disqualified on it.
